semantic_correction.stem: A parent is preparing powdered infant formula for a healthy full-term infant using a safe household water source. Which action is correct?

options.A: Measure the exact amount of water listed on the formula container first, then add the directed amount of powder.
options.B: Add extra water to each bottle to reduce the concentration and make the formula easier for the infant to tolerate.
options.C: Add extra powder when the infant seems hungry so each bottle provides more calories than the labeled mixture.
options.D: Estimate the water-to-powder ratio from bottle size instead of using the measurements on the formula container.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC formula-preparation guidance instructs caregivers to use the exact amount of water and formula listed on the container, measure the water first, and then add the formula powder. Intentional dilution can leave an infant without enough nutrition, while too little water can overconcentrate the formula, contribute to dehydration, and make the kidneys and digestive system work too hard. For a healthy full-term infant using a safe water source, the container directions should be followed exactly rather than changing the ratio.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Prepare powdered infant formula using the exact manufacturer-specified water-to-powder ratio, measuring water first and avoiding intentional dilution or concentration.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened and balanced the correct answer, retained the CDC water-first/exact-ratio preparation sequence, and rebuilt distractors around intentional dilution, concentration, and estimation without introducing a universal hot-water rule for healthy full-term infants.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: May 2026 formula-feeding guidance plus current powdered-formula preparation instructions
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — infant nutrition/home-care teaching
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests safe formula reconstitution using the exact labeled ratio and water-first sequence.

option_audit.A: Correct. CDC instructs caregivers to measure the exact labeled amount of water first and then add the directed powder.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Extra water can dilute nutrition and make the formula unsafe.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Extra powder changes the prescribed concentration and can contribute to dehydration and excessive renal/digestive workload.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The labeled measurements should be followed exactly rather than estimated from bottle size.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows the current CDC preparation sequence and exact-ratio requirement.
cueing_check: All four options are formula-preparation actions of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies A.
